newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-NFF welcomes moderation in Australian wages.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-NFF welcomes moderation in Australian wages.

text.p: The moderation in Australian wages growth was welcomed by the National Farmers Federation (NFF) on Thursday, saying it had opened the way for a further cut in interest rates.

However, Todd Ritchie, the NFF's director of economic policy, said in a statement that while the economy wide measure of wages had slowed, there was very little evidence of any moderation in enterprise bargaining, with some involving increases of more than 6.0 percent.
"This raises the concern, clearly identified by the Reserve Bank, that wages growth could accelerate once again when the economy recovers," he said.
Ritchie said the Reserve Bank also remained concerned about the Australian Council of Trade Union's (ACTU) "Living Wage" claim.

"If the Industrial Relation Commission was to grant the ACTU's application, it could account for wage increases of up to 20 percent in agriculture in the first year," he said, adding that such increase would have adverse effects on the Australian economy.

Figures released earlier on Thursday showed Australian average weekly ordinary time earnings (AWOTE) for adults employed full time rose 0.7 percent in the three months to August, seasonally adjusted for an annual rise of 3.5 percent. -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
